raw_response:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest radiographs demonstrate bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (enlarged hila on the PA view) and right paratracheal lymph node enlargement (widened right paratracheal stripe), which is the classic "1-2-3 sign" or Garland triad consistent with Stage I sarcoidosis. Stage I is defined by intrathoracic lymphadenopathy without pulmonary parenchymal infiltrates.
